summary.headline: APL Apollo Q2 FY27 volume hit 960,000 tons with EBITDA near Rs 6,000/ton; management guides FY27 EBITDA up 20%, with the 15% volume target conditional on Dubai and steel supply.
summary.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 its best quarter on volume, EBITDA and net profit, with volume of 960,000 tons despite UAE operations being disrupted, steel shortages in the domestic market and container disruption affecting exports. Growth came from the APL Apollo brand and roofing sheets, where pricing and EBITDA spreads improved, while low-margin SG Premium and export volumes were deliberately not pursued. Management guided FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis and said Q2 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 6,000 is sustainable. Working capital days were stated as zero, and cash rose 15% QoQ to Rs 16 billion. Several answers on Dubai, SG Premium and volume guidance were non-committal.

segments.name: APL Apollo brand
segments.commentary: Management says brand products get better pricing and EBITDA spreads; APL Apollo and roofing volume grew about 20% YoY in H1, with double-digit growth expected in H2. Analysts were told the brand targets 15-20% YoY growth.

segments.name: Roofing sheets
segments.commentary: Capacity cited at 7 lakh tons per year (about 175,000 tons per quarter); Q1 volume was about 135,000 tons and the target for the current quarter is 175,000 tons. Mix is 50% housing, 25% commercial/industrial and 25% other industrial; thickness 0.4-3.5 mm; no commission paid to third parties.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Low-margin product; management declined to give volume guidance due to steel shortage and low margin. Management said it can sell about 200,000 tons if steel prices fall and that absolute EBITDA would rise as volume increases.

segments.name: UAE (Dubai) operations
segments.commentary: Volume at about 40% of past levels; current run rate about 100,000 tons per year against about 300,000 tons capacity. Brownfield expansion to about 500,000 tons by March 2027, with EBITDA of Rs 8,000-10,000/ton expected on new mills. Management says no losses there.

segments.name: Defence, aerospace and specialised tubes
segments.commentary: New specialised tube mill can produce up to 250x250 mm with 16 mm thickness; samples sent to agencies, with results expected in 2-3 months. Development items for ISRO and DRDO are in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis by March 2027; management says it may beat this if UAE operations recover in H2. Management said absolute EBITDA should cross Rs 2,200 crore this year (one analyst cited Rs 2,200-2,300 crore; Shaleen Kumar's Rs 2,400 crore reference was given by management as possible if Dubai performed).

Apollo brand and roofing volume growth of about 15% for FY27 (about double-digit in H2); management also cited 15-20% YoY growth for these two segments. Company-wide volume guidance not committed due to Dubai and SG Premium uncertainty.
Q3 FY27 EBITDA per ton expected to be above Rs 6,000; October described as good and above guidance.

Management said FY28 EBITDA could reach about Rs 2,500 crore; in response to an analyst's Rs 3,000 crore scenario, management agreed it is achievable if Dubai, domestic steel supply and container freight stabilise. Management said that if it targets Rs 6,000-6,500/ton, it will update guidance after another quarter of evidence.
Capex target of 7 million tons greenfield plus brownfield capacity and 1 million tons de-bottlenecking within two years. Capex outflow in H2 expected to be about Rs 200 crore.
Net cash of about Rs 1,600 crore expected to rise to about Rs 2,300 crore; Rs 200-300 crore of this is earmarked for capex, and management will decide the use of the remainder later.
capex_capacity: Target of 7 million tons greenfield plus brownfield capacity and 1 million tons de-bottlenecking within the next two years (per management).
Current run-rate of 960,000 tons per quarter; utilisation about 70-75%.
Dubai capacity about 300,000 tons, rising to about 500,000 tons by March 2027 with two new mills; run-rate about 100,000 tons per year.
H1 FY27 capex Rs 400 crore; H2 capex expected to be low (about Rs 200 crore).
Greenfield additions described as small, limiting fixed-cost impact; brownfield expansion said not to hurt existing fixed costs materially.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for APL Apollo and roofing remains strong, with no decline seen, and that order books are full despite higher steel prices causing customers to delay quotations.
Pricing: black pipe price cited at about Rs 70,000/ton vs competitors at Rs 68,000-70,000; HR coil about Rs 60,000/ton; conversion cost about Rs 10/kg; worst item margin about Rs 6,000/ton.
Discounts: July required higher discounts; August and September needed less. A demand-driven discount swing can move results by Rs 10-15 crore per quarter.
Management said steel plant shutdowns are causing shortages, with November also weak and volumes expected to recover to about 400,000 tons per month from December.

Management said Q2 margin expansion came from three sources: exiting non-profitable volumes, roofing capacity additions and cost/innovation. It declined to give product-level EBITDA; the disclosure has been discontinued.
Exports affected by very high container freight; UAE exports blocked.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised FY27 volume guidance given H1 growth of about 4% vs an earlier 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15% guidance holds for the Apollo brand and roofing, but company-wide volume guidance is not committed because of Dubai and steel shortage; low-margin volumes are being deliberately dropped.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall QoQ, and why did the FD balance drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the other-income decline to FX gains and losses; the FD drop of about Rs 225 crore is due to reclassification of over-one-year FDs to within one year, and management said it would check the FX figure.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is Rs 6,000/ton EBITDA, and what if steel prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 6,000/ton is sustainable, citing the exit from non-profitable business, roofing additions, cost savings and utilisation of 70-75%. Management said SG Premium growth would dilute per-ton margin but lift absolute EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the drop in GP per ton when mix has improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said light structures carry lower realisation and GP; GP per ton fell about Rs 500/ton QoQ, and light-structure mix was about 25% in Q2 per management (analyst noted 35%).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the large volume jump from Q1 to Q2 beyond roofing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the APL Apollo brand, where the company shifted focus from SG Premium to Apollo branding and got better pricing, with Q3 seen as strong so far.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 EBITDA outlook, including Dubai recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 2,400 crore is achievable this year if Dubai performs, and agreed Rs 3,000 crore for FY28 is possible if Dubai, domestic steel supply and container freight stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Will falling rainfall affect housing demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said housing demand remains intact; any impact would be 2-4% at most, and order books and enquiries are strong.

risks_watch: Dubai/UAE operations remain largely shut: run-rate about 100,000 tons vs about 500,000 tons capacity after expansion, and management cannot commit on timing.
Steel shortage and plant shutdowns; November expected to be weak, with recovery from December.
Sustainability of Rs 6,000/ton EBITDA if HRC falls to Rs 55,000-60,000; management said it wants to see another quarter before raising FY28 guidance.
Adding about 2 million tons of capacity over the next one to one-and-a-half years with unclear fixed-cost impact.
Opacity: product-level EBITDA disclosure discontinued; SG Premium and heavy/super-heavy mix not quantified; a figure in slide 18 (H1 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 11,000) was acknowledged as a typo.
Freight and container disruption affecting exports; power cost at Rs 6.2-6.3/unit vs Rs 5 target.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the APL Apollo brand, roofing and EBITDA trajectory, citing October as above guidance and Q3 expected above Rs 6,000/ton. It was evasive on company-wide volume guidance, Dubai timing, SG Premium volumes and product-level EBITDA, repeatedly saying it could not commit or that the matter was outside its control.

adds.what: Dubai (UAE) brownfield expansion to ~500,000 tons/yr with two new mills (from ~300,000 tons)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 absolute EBITDA growth of about 20% and 15-20% growth for the APL Apollo brand and roofing, backed partly by roofing capacity (7 lakh t/yr, Q1 ~135k t to 175k t target), Dubai expansion to ~500k t by March 2027 and steady ~72.5% utilisation, but company-wide volume growth is not committed due to Dubai and steel supply uncertainty.
